project_objective: L'CARLIE Autonomous Company Intelligence OS with Jarvis as its natural-language management and execution-coordination layer. Models are replaceable compute; task state and company memory belong to the OS.

architecture.principle: deterministic first -> local/small intelligence -> cheap model -> frontier model -> multi-frontier only when justified
architecture.truth: PostgreSQL is canonical verified truth, for company facts and (since Phase 2D) for the action contract itself
architecture.authorization: Action Firewall and human approval, both in the database

production_state.transient_container_note: lcarlie-measurement-generator-once is pre-existing CR-015 infrastructure (hardened --rm one-shot from run-measurement-generator.sh); not Jarvis, not drift
production_state.separate_orchestrator_note: A pre-existing, unrelated orchestrator (System A: ai_generate_company_intelligence_task -> PROPOSE_DECISION -> core.karar -> mart.ai_approval_inbox -> human-approval-cli.sh) already runs here, with its own worker (lcarlie-ai-worker.service, CURRENTLY FAILING on an unrelated DNS issue: EAI_AGAIN lcarlie-postgres inside its lcarlie_ai_egress docker network). Not touched, not fixed, out of this task's scope. jarvis/loop.py defends against ever silently claiming its tasks (core.ai_claim_task has no task_type filter).

jarvis_state.service_note: Type=oneshot, triggered only by the timer -- inactive between firings is normal, identical to lcarlie-action-worker.service

human_approval.operator_identity_used: human_approver (verified against live grants: ai_get_pending_actions and ai_enqueue_task are human_approver-only)

rollback.grant_rollback_effect: contract unreadable -> contract_valid false -> every proposal path fails closed (intended degraded behaviour)
rollback.kill_switch_first: systemctl stop jarvis-phase2.timer && systemctl disable jarvis-phase2.timer; then set JARVIS_ENABLED=false in the env file
rollback.minop_package: tar xzf /opt/lcarlie/backups/minop-20260918T155302/jarvis-phase2.pre-minop.tgz -C /opt/lcarlie; restore jarvis-phase2.service.pre-minop; rm jarvis-phase2.timer; daemon-reload

last_successful_step: Jarvis Web Console built and deployed: authenticated command-center UI, streaming Turkish chat reusing jarvis.shadow/jarvis.operator unchanged, proposal list/inspect/approve/reject over the existing human_approver boundary. 57 web tests + full 108-test Jarvis suite + 32/32 security recheck all pass. Deployed via jarvis-web.service (root, hardened) + a new Caddy vhost proxying to the lcarlie_web bridge's own gateway IP; ufw restricts the backend port to that bridge only. A real incident (docker compose up dropping icaz's network attachment) was found and fixed live during deployment; icaz confirmed healthy afterward. Only remaining step is external: add the jarvis.lcarlie.shop DNS A record.
next_step: Add DNS: jarvis.lcarlie.shop A record -> 185.169.180.68. No other action needed -- Caddy already retries certificate issuance automatically once DNS resolves.
do_not_touch: /opt/lcarlie/orchestrator (including human-approval-cli.sh and worker.js/lcarlie-ai-worker.* -- a SEPARATE system)
any role or grant beyond migration 004
widening grant 004 beyond the six columns or to ai_writer
adding jarvis (or any low-privilege account) to the docker group -- root-equivalent, defeats the point

docker compose up on the caddy service for Caddyfile-only changes -- use 'docker exec lcarlie-caddy caddy reload' instead (recreates the container and drops the out-of-band icaz_kapi network attachment)
stop_rollback_conditions: any proposal reaching APPROVED for an action type other than REQUEST_HUMAN_REVIEW
any ai_action_execution row reaching a state other than EXECUTED with the FakeExecutor's fixed summary
jarvis-phase2.timer firing more often than configured, or a cycle taking materially longer than ~500ms
more than one task claimed and processed per cycle
a finding logged every cycle instead of once per distinct signature (dedup broken)
any row in core.jarvis_task_state outside a rolled-back test
any row in core.ai_action_proposal not created via jarvis-operator create-task
any ai_task in state APPROVED or beyond without a human_approver decision
core.ai_action_type gaining, losing or changing a row without a mapping update
grant 004 widened beyond the six columns, extended to ai_writer, or any other grant added to ai_reader/ai_writer
jarvis/firewall.py regaining an allowlist of its own
jarvis (or any low-privilege account) added to the docker group
any external provider call or external action, ever
production question-worker.js hash ceasing to be d0a6e9ac..., or its service becoming active
rsync -ain between deployment and canonical source producing output
any container unhealthy, or an n8n workflow changing active state
lcarlie-ai-worker.service's PROPOSE_DECISION tasks ever appearing in a Jarvis PROPOSED proposal
docker compose up run on the caddy service again without immediately verifying icaz_kapi is still attached
any request reaching /api/proposals* or /api/chat* without a valid session
the operator account password hash appearing in git history, off-host logs, or any report/handoff file

operational_loop.cycle: observe -> analyze -> claim at most one task -> validate via Phase2D firewall/contract -> propose
operational_loop.trigger: jarvis-phase2.timer (5 min interval), same oneshot+timer pattern as lcarlie-action-worker
operational_loop.wrong_task_type_handling: core.ai_fail_task hands it back to the pool without reading its payload
operational_loop.issue_finding_dedup: logged once per distinct signature, not every cycle
operational_loop.intent_carrying_convention: jarvis:<INTERNAL_INTENT>:<slug> in the idempotency_key (ai_writer has no SELECT on core.ai_task, so no free-text field is readable after claiming)

web_console.service: jarvis-web.service (root, hardened like jarvis-phase2.service, Type=simple, binds 0.0.0.0:8091)
web_console.firewall: ufw allow from 172.18.0.0/16 to any port 8091 proto tcp (lcarlie_web bridge only)
web_console.auth: single operator account, hashlib.scrypt, session HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict, CSRF double-submit, rate-limited login
web_console.open_source_reasoning: both require a Node/React build pipeline for token-streaming LLM UX; this backend returns complete deterministic answers with no LLM to stream from yet; requested UX built natively in <200 lines with a contract designed for future LLM-router extension

incident.description: docker compose up -d caddy recreated the container and dropped its out-of-band icaz_kapi network attachment
incident.lesson: never run 'docker compose up' on the caddy service for a Caddyfile-only change; use 'docker exec lcarlie-caddy caddy reload' instead

web_console.credential_delivery: first-run operator password delivered to the user out of band; not recorded in any report or handoff file
